item.title: Change the sequence?
item.content:encoded: After reading this I was left with the thought that leading with the content of Policy Directive K-23396-D6 formatted as an SCP (obviously a very short one) followed by the still-collapsed Former Containment Documentation would present the payoff more effectively. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Meh, I upvoted because I like the idea. Execution might have some flaws, but I'm not sure it's even possible to correct them.

Starting from the surface… clearly 920 wrote the note itself to escape containment. But it did that from containment, so why would it bother? Obviously the containment is not working. All 920 accomplished was revealing the fact that containment wasn't working, because I would assume that the Foundation is smart enough to know that the note is a fake. However, if we don't see the note, we don't get the full picture. So let's also assume that the note was written during a temporary containment breach, and that was the only opportunity 920 had to write it.

The next assumption is that the EX classification is faked as well, but only present on the "website", which is under 920's domain. But if that's the case, it would be more successful if it simply deleted all records of itself from even existing at the Foundation, thus meaning there would be no page about it at all. Of course, then we wouldn't get to read it, so that's a self-defeating paradox. Aside from the fact that physical copies would still exist, so it'd be a failure of a plan anyway.

So the next assumption is that the this website isn't literally a website in-universe, but just the method by which the documents are conveyed to us, including documents that don't exist in digital format. But in that case, they wouldn't have been edited by 920, and thus this wouldn't be an EX.

So the only possibilities I see for 920 are that the Foundation really is retarded and was fooled by the note, in which case it "works" as is; or the EX needs to be removed and this added to the main list, with this included as a failed attempt to breach containment. The former is clearly already resulting in many downvotes. The latter would make the item a lot less threatening, and might not get the desired upvotes.

The only third possibility would require coming up with an extremely convoluted, subtle, believable plan executed by 920 that doesn't make the Foundation seem retarded, explains why any documentation of its former effects exists at all, and still conveys the fact that this item tricked the Foundation into letting it out and classifying it as EX. It would probably require rewriting the entire page and coming up with something more elaborate than a single email.

But as I said, the idea itself already got my upvote. I hope you can work out the issues to get more upvotes from the people with higher standards.

I actually prefer the Foundation when it's reminded that it's not some shadowy, infallible organization of Men in Black, but composed of actual people — people who make mistakes and jokes and fail and sometimes do stupid things… but this is a little too far in that direction. This thing had valid, working containment protocols and a set of defined powers that would lead anyone remotely competent to be suspect of the method by which it subverted them, but it still apparently worked. The whole thing reeks of (as much as I tend to hate the label) lolfoundation and Mary-Sue-ism from the author's super-special pet printer that's smarter than the whole foundation.
